chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Ma'mar ibn Yahya and Isma'il, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

He gives one taslim, whether he is an Imam or otherwise. The proper way regarding this report is that we understand it to mean when the follower has no one on his left, as he explained in the narration of Mansur ibn Hazim and 'Anbasah ibn Mus'ab; and what follows further clarifies that.

key_terms.الْمَأْمُومُ: the follower praying behind the Imam
key_terms.الْوَجْهُ: the sound interpretive approach to the report
key_terms.تَسْلِيمَةً وَاحِدَةً: a single salutation concluding the prayer
key_terms.رِوَايَةِ: a transmitted narration used for clarification
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: he gives the taslim at the end of salat

ai.seo_question: When is a single taslim sufficient in salat according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the fiqh of taslim in salat, stating that one taslim may suffice whether the person is the Imam or not. It then explains that this report should be understood in a specific case: when the ma'mum has no one on his left side, in harmony with other narrations.
